title: Valid UTF-8 input chunked inside a multibyte sequence
summary: A valid UTF-8 input, containing a key after multibyte text, divided into chunks whose boundaries fall inside the multibyte sequences (and, separately, at every byte).
rationale: Chunking is a fact about how valid content is delivered, not a transformation of it: the bytes, the secret span and the batch reading are the same whatever the boundaries. A UTF-8 byte boundary inside a 2-, 3- or 4-byte sequence is valid for a byte stream; the same split of a string would be a different question (see unicode-input-rejected-before-scanning). What a stream API does with it is the product's assertion.

expectation.rationale: Project policy: the chunk boundaries do not change what is expected; the input is valid and the key bytes are the secret, at the same offsets as the unchunked input. Reverse if a maintainer decides chunked delivery has its own expectation.

sources.supports: Section 3 table: U+0800-U+FFFF encodes as three bytes and U+10000-U+10FFFF as four, so every zero-width, BOM and emoji offset shift in these fixtures is derivable from the code point.
UTF-8 decode: BOM bytes are consumed by decode; invalid sequences become U+FFFD; a streaming TextDecoder keeps an incomplete multibyte sequence buffered across chunks.
sources.locator: sections 6.1, 7.2 and 8.1.1 (Living Standard, last updated 21 May 2026)

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Research for #96 (parent #92). Synthetic fixtures only; input facts and expectations live here, while stream APIs, limits, actual output and rejection assertions belong to downstream engine and product regression populations.
